mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a contraction in economic demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 declined by more than 1% over the last quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in the last month signals a surge in supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS decline > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS declined by more than 100,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals an inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% in the last quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in the last two months, it signals a robust economic expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% in 3 months and HOUST increase > 10% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% in the last quarter and HOUST increased by more than 10% in the last two months.
